featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova – Authentic South Indian Delight!

Visited **Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova** on Sunday with a group of 12, and the experience was fantastic!

The **Chicken Ghee Roast, Chicken Chintamani, and Pepper Chicken** were absolutely outstanding - rich, spicy, and packed with authentic South Indian flavors. 🍗🔥
We also loved the **Malabar Parotta, Appam, Idiyappam, and Dosa with Sambar** - soft, fresh, and perfect with the curries.

Veg dishes like **Jackfruit Cutlet and Jackfruit Biryani** were surprisingly delicious, and the **Chicken Biryani** was aromatic and generously portioned. The **Mango Mint Cooler** was a refreshing highlight after the spicy feast. 🥭❄️

If the main seating area is full, they have **additional seating inside WTF**, which is very convenient during peak hours.
They also offer a **tasting platter where the staff explains different curries and how they are used in cooking** - a brilliant concept for first-time visitors and food enthusiasts.

The restaurant is **just ~500 meters from Versova Metro Station**, making it very easy to reach. 🚇

For around **₹9.7K for 12 people (~₹800 per person)**, the quality, quantity, and taste were totally worth it.

**Highly recommended for authentic South Indian food and group outings! Will definitely visit again.**

#TanjoreTiffinRoom #SouthIndianFood #VersovaEats #MumbaiFoodies #AndheriWest #FoodReview #BiryaniLovers #ParottaLove #MetroFriendly #FoodieLife

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is quite popular and is usually packed during both lunch and dinner, so making a reservation is a must. This was my second visit here, and of course we ordered their signature Railway Curry it never disappoints.

This time we also tried:
Mutton Cutlet
Mini Idlis
Veg Cutlet
Beef Roast with Lemon Rice
Egg Appams
Fried prawns

The mini idlis with ghee were absolutely delicious, and the beef roast was our next favourite.
Fried prawns was crispy and had a balanced taste.

I had high expectations from the mutton cutlet, but it didn’t quite live up to the hype. The lemon rice and egg appam were also slightly on the sweeter side, which didn’t go too well with our palate.

Their chutneys are amazing though definitely a highlight!

The staff is extremely warm and courteous, and the ambience is lovely. They even have a pet dog at the restaurant, but do be careful as it may suddenly run up or try to bite if you get too close.

Overall, a charming place with great service and some standout dishes, but a few items could be improved taste-wise.

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

featured_reviews.name: Mudit Bansal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

My absolute favorite was the Benne Podi Masala Dosa. It’s not like the traditional benne dosa that comes drenched in coconut oil—this version is neat, easy to eat, and definitely feels healthier. The filter coffee was comforting and well brewed, and the appam was soft and light. They have a wide range of South Indian delicacies on the menu, and there’s a lot more I’m looking forward to trying.
I’ll definitely keep updating my reviews as and when we visit again. For now, the Benne Podi Masala Dosa is completely on my mind and a must-try! 😋

featured_reviews.name: Yati Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic, no-frills South Indian food in Juhu, Sri Annapoorna Cafe is an absolute gem. The menu is refreshingly simple, but every item delivers on taste, quality, and authenticity.

The sambhar is rich, perfectly spiced, and feels like it’s straight out of a traditional South Indian kitchen. The benne podi masala dosa is a standout—crispy on the outside, generously layered with butter, and packed with flavorful podi that hits just right.

The idli with rasam is comfort in a plate—soft, fluffy idlis paired with a tangy, soul-warming rasam that you’ll want to keep sipping. And the vada? Crisp on the outside, soft inside, and absolutely worth the hype.

What really sets this place apart is how it sticks to its roots—no unnecessary gimmicks, just honest, traditional flavors done right. Add to that the pocket-friendly pricing, and you’ve got a spot that’s truly worth every rupee.

Simple menu, authentic taste, and consistently good food—definitely a must-visit for South Indian lovers.

Why is Nandu Dosas the best place in Mumbai to have dosas?

We all know that there are 100s of best places in Mumbai for dosas, but this one is beyond the best. It is simply so fine and tasty that even the best places seem dull in front of it. The place we are talking about is Nandu Dosa, located behind Ritumbara College, Vile Parle.

Read below to find out what makes Nandu Dosa one of the best dosa places in Mumbai.

Sizzling Cheese Jinni Dosa
Nandu Dosa is famous for its Jinni Cheese Dosa, which is crispy in nature, stuffed with vegetables such as carrots, cabbage, and capsicum, adding spiciness and sweetness to the tangy, rich Schezwan sauce.
Bet it’s so tasty that you would order another one as you cannot resist its saucy nature and cheese-filled goodness.

Made with Fresh Batter
Nandu dosas are fresh in nature because the batter itself is made early in the morning, preserving its freshness for the whole day so that it doesn’t get spoiled.
If you try the idli as well, it still holds the freshness which feels like it was recently made — so yum, so tasty.

Its Famous Red Chutney
So sweet, so spicy — just tasting like a wow!
Yes, Nandu’s orange chutney is an absolute wow, made with cheese and chutney which has a sweet and spicy taste. Filled with red chili, tamarind, and roasted chana dal, it adds a perfect blend to the Jinni dosas.

Pro Tip
If you have an angry girlfriend and want to make her happy, take her to Nandu Dosas and order the Cheese Jinni Dosa.
See how her anger melts from anguish to just like the sweet orange chutney. This is one of the best ways to make her heart go from "hmm" to "uhmmm".

Nandu Dosas has a variety of dosas, but I would highly recommend trying the Jinni Dosa and Paneer Mysore Dosa, as these are the best-selling options and are always in high demand. They carry the authentic taste of South India while adding more variations to the South Indian culinary experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re visiting Mumbai and searching for the best South Indian breakfast in Juhu, you cannot miss Benne Heritage Bangalore Dosa.

This place truly has a hype of its own — and after experiencing it firsthand, I can confidently say it deserves every bit of it.

As a North Indian, I had never even heard of a “Benne Dosa” before my trip. But the buzz around this spot was so strong among locals that I felt compelled to try it.

I arrived in the morning and ended up standing in line for nearly an hour just to get in — which might sound intense, but the experience began impressing me even before I entered. The staff personally came to people waiting in line, thanked us for our patience, and even offered sweets. That level of hospitality instantly set the tone and showed how much they value their customers.

Inside, the place is lively, energetic, and completely packed. This is not a traditional sit-down restaurant; most guests stand and eat, with designated tables only for elderly guests, pregnant women, small children, or those with medical conditions.

Ordering is fully digital through self-service screens — you select your items, pay, and receive a token. There’s also a glass-panel view of the kitchen so you can watch your food being freshly prepared, which adds to the authenticity and excitement. When your token appears, you collect your order downstairs and enjoy your meal.

On recommendation from regular customers there, I ordered the Benne Plain Dosa, Benne Masala Dosa, Donne Biryani, and Cold filter Coffee — and honestly, this turned out to be the most heavenly South Indian meal I’ve ever had anywhere, whether in India or abroad. The flavors were outstanding, the texture perfect, and every bite felt worth the wait. The iced filter coffee alone is reason enough to visit.

Another plus point: it’s surprisingly affordable. Most dosas range between ₹100–₹200, making it one of the best value-for-money food experiences in Mumbai.

They don’t deliver via Swiggy or Zomato, so you must visit in person — but trust me, that’s part of the charm. If you’re already going there, you might as well dine in and soak in the full experience.

Final verdict: If you love authentic South Indian food or are a food tourist exploring Mumbai, this place is an absolute must-visit.

Long queue or not, I would gladly wait again just to relive this meal. Without a doubt, this is my favorite South Indian food spot on earth so far.

Highly, highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Ishita Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If comfort food had a personality, it would probably be Benne in Juhu. Benne - Heritage Bangalore Dosa has mastered the art of making South Indian food feel indulgent, nostalgic, and ridiculously satisfying all at once.

The star of the meal for me was easily the thatte idli - soft, fluffy, drenched in ghee, coated generously with podi masala, and honestly the kind of dish that instantly hits the spot. Every bite felt rich, comforting, and packed with flavour without trying too hard.

The dosas here deserve all the hype they’ve been getting across Mumbai food circles. I tried the Benne plain dosa, masala dosa, podi masala dosa, and garlic dosa - and somehow each one had a completely different personality. Crisp edges, buttery centres, perfect fermentation, and that signature Bangalore-style benne flavour that keeps lingering long after the meal ends. The chutneys deserve their own fanbase honestly - fresh, balanced, and addictive enough to want extra servings every single time.

The medu vadas were another standout - beautifully crisp on the outside, soft and airy inside, exactly how a good vada should be. And then came the filter coffee ice cream from their collab with Indu Ice Creams, which genuinely felt like the perfect ending to the meal. Creamy, strong coffee notes, slightly nostalgic, and an absolute must-try.

The space itself has a very minimal yet aesthetic South Indian café vibe - warm lighting, clean interiors, subtle Bangalore darshini-inspired energy, and an atmosphere that somehow feels both trendy and comforting together. A lot of diners online consistently rave about the crispy dosas, fresh chutneys, and ambience, and after visiting, it’s very easy to understand the obsession.

Overall, Benne feels less like just another dosa place and more like a love letter to Bangalore-style comfort food - buttery, soulful, and dangerously addictive.

Visited this Benne Dosa spot in Juhu recently, and it definitely lives up to its growing popularity. The place has a very casual, street-style vibe and is almost always buzzing with people. If you’re planning to visit, keep in mind that it gets quite crowded—especially during weekends and evening hours—so you might have to wait a bit before getting your order.

Coming to the food, we tried the Benne Masala Dosa and it was the clear standout. Perfectly crisp on the outside, soft inside, and generously coated with butter, it had that rich, authentic flavor you expect from a good benne dosa. The potato filling was well-seasoned and complemented the dosa really well.

We also ordered the Thatte Idli, which was decent but didn’t quite match up to the dosa. It was soft and fresh, but the overall taste felt a bit average compared to the highlight dish.

The filter coffee was served strong—maybe a bit too strong for my liking—so if you prefer a milder coffee, that’s something to keep in mind.

Overall, it’s a great place to satisfy your South Indian cravings, especially if you’re going specifically for the benne dosa. Just try to avoid peak hours if you want a more relaxed experience.

**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”

Arya Bhavan Run by Muthuswamy this Restaurant has opened in the recent past at Vile Parle east relatively new to western suburbs i have been eating at the OG Matunga outlet bang opp Matunga central Railway Station close to 2 decades now

1.This is the run and owned  by the same family who runs the matunga eatery since day one it opened in vile parle east i started frequenting this place  I must clearly point out my observations for this place
Food is not as perfected like the OG Arya bhavan at matunga i feel that  matunga  has good chefs and service staff to deliver Excellence this vile parle branch offers almost the same menu  but at  times I felt that the food goes haywire chutneys sometimes  are very  well prepared  but some times watery chutneys and half done dosas not done right.

2.i feel  owner should & MUST visit this place atleast 3 times a week though his son and the owner himself know me i feel the service and food here get wonky many  times as they have recently expanded to other branches in sewri chembur too hence staff issue remains a challenge in kitchen as well in service.

3.So the rating 3 is given in comparison with the Original Matunga Arya Bhavan the food otherwise is amazing rite from the masala dosa perfectly made to the Medu vada -is Must try make sure they freshly make it for you when u order it the best perfect medu vada i have ever eaten in mumbai (matunga branch does it right each time everytime) they serve the amazing red green thick freshly made chutneys and perfectly made Sambhar

Thathe idli with podi is perfect

Another hidden gem in the menu is Biscuit Dosa its heaven specially if u like pizzas u will like this Innovatively made dosa styled and made by them.

Idlis are well made nice fluffy perfected with their in-house spl batter u will notice the difference in the first bite itself

They have other variety of dosas like palak dosa Mysore dosa which go well select ur pick

Kanchipuram idli Brahman idli all are good

The best part is they have full ac Restaurant with table service

The service is wobbly which I have complained to the owner once as you have to keep asking people to clean table for water for your food to be served hence I rate service 2star as the staff training is a challenge here getting staff is a bigger challenge in this place hence if they have full strength of staff you might get proper service sometimes they will forget chutneys with dosas hence you will have to ask them for chutneys by the time they get chutney dosa will be over the person who cleans tables may not clean the table properly you may have to ask again for it constantly you will have to ask for water tissue spoon etc ....they may not be proactive it all depends on the staff mood so

While ac works fine washroom is a challenge to use as water soap tissues hygeine are clear issues which owner has to address ASAP

this place  is way above the average south indian Udupi restaurants and its can be termed as a gem for south indian breakfast lovers it does decent "ghati" desi style pizza too few sandwiches freshly made juices and has started chaats

Showstopper is the goti sodas with flavours ,Ananda milk is stocked up and has handmade ice cream which  could definitely be tried chocolate Orange my personal favorite

Coin idli ,butter idli, are all time favorite

Rassam wada is another gem in their menu but have it with pipping hot rasam  and freshly made vada

Their tomato Rasam served here is another favourite's I sometimes come here just to have that however matunga outlet  does it better

Filter coffee is decent served in traditional brass tumbler set with spl sugar

Parking is roadside avoid going on weekends public holidays

Must visit the place after 8.30am before noon on weekdays to avoid  any waiting reservation is not required they are there on swiggy zomato however eating food going there is recommended

Curd rice, bisse bille bhat pav bhaji all is served

Looking for variety seated service with ac  quality food  this is it!!

Arya Bhavan by Muthuswamy Caterers in Vile Parle is truly a hidden gem for anyone who loves authentic South Indian cuisine. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures that guests are well taken care of.

We tried the classic Rava Dosa, Medu Vada, and Filter Coffee, and each item was a burst of flavour. The sambar and chutneys were fresh, aromatic, and perfectly complemented the dishes. The Mini Meals Thali is also a must-try – it offers a great variety of items and feels like a complete homemade meal, full of comfort and taste.

What makes Arya Bhavan stand out is the quality and consistency. The ingredients taste fresh, the hygiene is commendable, and every dish carries the legacy of the Muthuswamy brand. Whether you're visiting for breakfast, lunch, or just a coffee break – this place never disappoints.

It’s no surprise that this place is loved by foodies and families alike. Highly recommended for anyone looking for genuine, soulful South Indian food in Mumbai!

featured_reviews.name: Suhas Kulkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
An Exceptionally Great Breakfast experience for us at this restaurant!

Very neat and tidy but clean place, with only four tables on the ground floor and probably another four on the first floor. Very simple interior and ambience that makes us feel at ease.

Very good service by a very efficient person Tiwari ji who is always on the move and taking care of every person on every table, without a need to call again and remind for anything. A very humble person with smiling face, Tiwari ji caters to all our requests with full energy throughout. He is Occasionally assisted or supported by the owner of the place who supervises all activities, in the kitchen and with the guests alike.

Now, coming to the food part, a really awesome experience I would say.

An humble Upma, tasted so nice, making me to say it was one of the best Upmas I must have eaten outside. Everything was so impeccable with its looks, texture, taste and it was doubly complimented by the Coconut Chutney served alongwith it.

Rasam Vada with Chutney was another great thing to savour, no complaints on it.

The Star of the show was Button Idly with Srilankan Curry -  something I am short of words to appreciate and explain. Sambhar replaced by Coconut based gravy in a bowl and button idlys immersed in them, so that they absorb all the flavours of the gravy within them, each bite of every piece of the Idly kept us craving for more! A very great and unique experience for us.

All this ended with a supurb dose of Filter Coffee, customised to our choice of regular or strong and that really left us super satisfied.

There is no parking available here, one has use the Pay and Parking place of the shopping mall just adjesannt to this place.

Overall, a must visit place if we happen to be in this area anytime. One may need to wait for tables, for its being occupied with people who are in no hurry while enjoying the food here!

featured_reviews.name: Prabinsum
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was a company audit done today by me and we posed as customers. Too many complains. Owners can take this as an advise in order to improvise.

1. Don't play music so loud that visitors find it difficult to talk. And if at all music is played don't connect your paytm payment notification tones and phone call rings on the same player. It's really annoying to hear your phone ringtones on speakers and also I'm not interested to know how much my next table person is paying.

2. Put curtains in the ac room. Ac cooling effect will be more and also too much harsh sun light coming inside. It's good if you have greenery outside. There you just have scorching sun. So better cover the glass.

3. When you have sugar packets on the table, then why waiter is asking wether we want with sugar or without sugar. It's improper customer service training. Train the waiters.

4. Make sure the menu has basic things. Being a south Indian Brahmin cafe if you don't have idli, it's not right. You have thatte idli but keep steamed idlis too.

5. Right after bill amount was received, the waiter immediately asked us - "aapka hogaya kya" he din't even wait for a second to ask this question which was unexpected and rude. Again lack of customer service skills. Respect your customers.

6. The staircase is too narrow and I understand. The interiors are nice. Place is well utilised. Hats off to that but when customers are already climbing down and waiter can see it, he should step down, he stood there like a pillar and we had to literally sqeeze and go through him and pass downwards. He should realise manners when there are female customers.

These small and simple things make huge difference. There may be customers who don't bother about all this but even 1% of dissatisfaction should not exist in any business.

Thank you !
